scope: Focused follow-up on public-key s5 documents whose Table 20 StmF and StrF name different crypt filters; source-premise and reader-consumer audit only, not a complete public-key handler audit.

primary.text_effect: StmF is the default filter for streams and StrF is the default filter for strings. Each is independently optional, independently names a CF key or standard filter, and independently defaults to Identity. No rule requires these names to match.
Each supported crypt filter name has its corresponding file-encryption key; a reader may cache the key for streams using the same filter.
For a filter referenced from StmF or StrF, Recipients is an array of CMS byte strings. Only a filter referenced from a stream Crypt decode-parameter dictionary uses one CMS string.
s5 is the permitted public-key form when crypt filters are used; the recipient CMS yields seed and permissions, and the relevant recipient-array bytes participate in the per-key digest.

implementation: crates/pdf-syntax/src/crypt/public_key.rs::filter_lists chooses StmF, or StrF only when StmF is Identity, as the single document-level recipient list.

The loop over other CF dictionaries treats every other recipient-bearing filter as a stream-local filter and requires its Recipients entry to be a single string; a conforming distinct StrF recipient array is therefore rejected as UnsupportedEncryption.

crates/pdf-syntax/src/crypt.rs::Encryption stores one document key for both string and stream decryptions; `document/encryption.rs` routes strings through string_method() with that common key. Separate own_keys exist only for stream Crypt decode-parameter filters.
A conforming fixture with distinct StmF and StrF arrays and distinct seed-derived keys should therefore distinguish both parser acceptance and per-type key selection.
expected_assertions: Both PDFs open with the checked-in testnutzer certificate/key, require no recovery, and have no cut xref chain.
In both PDFs, the page content stream yields literal text `Stream key` and Catalog /Lang yields literal bytes `fr-FR`.
The shared-default control has a single CF name and one recipient array used as both StmF and StrF; its string and stream are encrypted under the same derived file key but their distinct object keys.
The target names different StmF and StrF CFs, each with its own valid Recipients array and a distinct seed-derived key.
validity_controls: Use PDF 1.7, V=4, SubFilter adbe.pkcs7.s5, two named AESV2 CF dictionaries, and each named as its own Table 20 default.
Each default filter has a one-item Recipients array containing a genuine OpenSSL CMS EnvelopedData object for the same recipient, with its own 20-byte seed and the same permission word.

Derive independent AESV2 file keys as first 16 bytes of SHA-1(seed || that filter's CMS DER), then apply Algorithm 1's object-specific key derivation and AES-CBC IV/padding for object 4 stream and object 1 string.
The draft asserts exact xref and no recovery, plus positive plaintext at both consumers. No malformed-input refusal claim is involved.
limitations: B57 records the executed rejection. Downstream distinct-key assertions cannot yet execute because opening fails.

Independent verifier decrypts CMS and AES payloads extracted from retained PDF bytes, not just regenerated ciphertext. Uses OpenSSL and independently derived keys; no external PDF-reader conformance certification.
qpdf --check exits at unsupported Adobe.PubSec; it is explicitly not treated as a successful syntax or encryption validator.
This case does not address different recipients/permissions across the two defaults, crypt-filter access timing, embedded-file defaults, or all SubFilter/V combinations.
